reason: Closure holds; I could not refute it. The numbers reproduce exactly from scratchpad r12/agg_out.json (56 exp60 x138 clips, official eval, clip bootstrap). z-edge drop: -0.00285 [-0.00461,-0.00136]. xy band <4 px (1.625 um): -0.01318 [-0.01624,-0.01010], W/L 13/43, dTP -862. Both CIs exclude 0 in both embryos. The strongest refutation attempt fails: 'sparse annotation turns borders into free bonus on a private embryo'. In 44b6, the sparsest lab embryo (base 0.79% matched), the xy band is only 0.127% matched (25/19,749). That is already BELOW the old absolute 0.16-0.3% break-even, yet the drop still loses: -0.00413 [-0.00788,-0.00085]. The z-edge drop there is -0.00655 [-0.01346,-0.00029]. Break-even is density-relative, because node value = 0.1*J*D/Nest (hyp_nodes-metric.notes.md l.4) and so shrinks with annotation density. It needs a border rate about 10x below the embryo's own base; measured is 6x (44b6) and 3x (6bba). One wording flaw: '3-8x above break-even' is a pooled figure dominated by 6bba and is false as an absolute statement for 44b6. The conclusion is unaffected. Minor: zedge wins on most clips (38/18) but loses the D-weighted mean the metric uses. Feasibility: no mechanism is proposed; the action is closure only, so R8, a dummy and a user OK do not apply and the finals are not affected. A narrower band or threshold search would be a post-hoc knob ladder on the lab and is not warranted at pooled -0.013.
